隷.meaning: A <part>gentleman</part> once promised to keep the village <part>altar</part> spotless. Now he can't stop: he mops at dawn, at midnight, even in his sleep, and the <part>mop</part> never leaves his hand. Polite to everyone, but a <kanji>slave</kanji> to his mop.
隷.on: When a gliding <sound>ray</sound> splashes up from the temple pond, he mops the splash before it lands.
隷.kun: His cat follows every stroke: <sound>she</sound> licks up a <sound>ta</sound>co crumb, sniffs the <sound>ga</sound>rlic in the bucket and pads on behind him.

拐.meaning: Pirates lower their <part>anchor</part> through a lighthouse window at night, hook the keeper's beloved teddy bear and stuff a cookie in its <part>mouth</part> so it won't squeak. Their captain waves a <part>sword</part> at the moon as they sail off. In the morning, a ransom note: they <kanji>kidnap</kanji> teddies.
拐.on: The keeper chases them across the bay in a dinghy towed by a giant <sound>ki</sound>te.

杉.meaning: A barber climbs the tallest <part>tree</part> in the forest and trims the shaggy green <part>whiskers</part> drooping from its branches. The trimmings smell so sweet that the whole town lines its drawers with them. The tree is a <kanji>cedar</kanji>.
杉.on: As a tip, the tree drops a tiny cone into his ice cream <sound>sun</sound>dae.
杉.kun: He wraps the trimmings round his <sound>su</sound>shi lunch, and a flock of <sound>gee</sound>se swoops down and steals the lot.

喉.meaning: The <part>marquis</part> sings opera every night, and one day a moth moves in. When he opens his <part>mouth</part> wide for the high note, out flutters the moth, yawning, after a cosy day deep in his <kanji>throat</kanji>.
喉.on: To soothe it afterwards, he licks an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne very slowly.
喉.kun: '<sound>No</sound>t again,' he croaks the next night, as a <sound>do</sound>lphin in the front row shouts for an encore.

衷.meaning: A tailor sews a <part>garment</part> with a pocket inside a pocket inside a pocket. In the very last one, on a tiny <part>pole</part>, sits a little <part>mouth</part> that whispers the owner's secret wishes. Only he can hear it, from his <kanji>inmost</kanji> pocket.
衷.on: It only goes quiet when he feeds it a piece of <sound>chew</sound>ing gum.

潟.meaning: A giant cooking on the beach sets his stone <part>mortar</part> on <part>hot coals</part> and <part>wrap</part>s a sail over it for a lid. Then he forgets it. The tide splashes in, <part>water drops</part> fill it to the brim, and it becomes a warm, still pool cut off from the waves: a <kanji>lagoon</kanji>.
潟.on: Flamingos split the lagoon up like a pie chart, each bird guarding its own <sound>sec</sound>tor.
潟.kun: In the middle, a big <sound>ca</sound>rp swims slow circles, nibbling a lost <sound>ta</sound>co.

臆.meaning: An astronaut on the <part>moon</part> has a grand <part>idea</part>: plant a flag on the far side. Then a crater creaks, and she hides behind the lander for an hour, flag trembling. Big ideas, tiny courage: that's <kanji>timidity</kanji>.
臆.on: A tiny <sound>oc</sound>topus in a fishbowl helmet bounces past and waves, and she shrieks.
臆.kun: Back at base she hides behind a toy <sound>moo</sound>se, a butterfly <sound>ne</sound>t pressed flat against her ribs: her chest.

羨.meaning: On a hot day, a woolly <part>sheep</part> watches her freshly shorn friend skip through the <part>water drops</part> of a garden sprinkler. She gives a big, bored <part>yawn</part>, as if she doesn't care, but she's sweltering under all that wool and very <kanji>envious</kanji>.
羨.on: A <sound>sen</sound>try guards the sprinkler and won't let her in without a haircut.
羨.kun: '<sound>Oo</sound>h,' she groans, as the shorn sheep cools off with a bowl of iced <sound>ra</sound>men in the shady <sound>ya</sound>rd.

麺.meaning: A bandit in a <part>mask</part> raids a <part>barley</part> field at midnight. Back at his hideout he grinds the grain, kneads it, and pulls it into long, wobbly strings, then slurps the lot. The bandit just really wanted <kanji>noodles</kanji>.
麺.on: The next night he hangs a <sound>men</sound>u on his hideout door.
麺.kun: His first customers are a <sound>moo</sound>se, a pair of <sound>gee</sound>se and a sleepy <sound>ko</sound>ala, all dusted white with flour.

朴.meaning: The village can't afford a fountain, so they hammer a rusty <part>faucet</part> straight into the trunk of an old <part>tree</part>. Turn it, and cool water dribbles out. No pipes, no pump, no paint: it's <kanji>crude</kanji>, but it works.
朴.on: A thirsty <sound>box</sound>er dog stands on its back legs to lap from it.
朴.kun: Someone screws a garden <sound>ho</sound>se onto it, and the old tree bursts into big white blossoms: a magnolia.

酌.meaning: At a mining-camp saloon, the bartender keeps the drinks in an old <part>dynamite</part> crate and serves them with a tin <part>scoop</part>, one ladle per cup, never spilling a drop, even when the floor shakes. Miners call it the best <kanji>bar-tending</kanji> in the hills.
酌.on: Her tip jar is a glass <sound>shark</sound> with its jaws wide open.
酌.kun: When the barrel runs dry, the camp <sound>coo</sound>k dips the same scoop into the river.

茎.meaning: A <part>tumbleweed</part> rolls across the desert and snags on one thin blade of <part>grass</part> that refuses to bend. The wind howls and the tumbleweed spins round and round it like a ring on a finger, but that skinny green <kanji>stalk</kanji> holds.
茎.on: A beetle uses it as the candle on its birthday <sound>ca</sound>ke.
茎.kun: A <sound>cu</sound>ckoo lands on top and pecks at a <sound>ki</sound>wi speared on the tip.

餌.meaning: A fox dangles a plate of <part>food</part> on a string outside a rabbit hole. Out pops one long <part>ear</part>, twitching, then a nose, and in a flash the rabbit grabs the plate and is gone. It was meant as bait, but now it's just the rabbit's <kanji>food</kanji>.
餌.on: The fox sulks off and drives home in his muddy <sound>jee</sound>p.
餌.kun: '<sound>Eh</sound>?' he grunts, finding only a scrap of <sound>sa</sound>ri silk tied where the plate was.

虹.meaning: An <part>insect</part> carpenter at her tiny <part>workbench</part> glues seven strips of coloured wing film, red to violet, into one curving bridge. She props it over a puddle so the ants can cross in style: a <kanji>rainbow</kanji>.
虹.on: At the far end, a beetle sells a striped ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne in all seven colours.
虹.kun: A grasshopper slides down it, scrapes its <sound>knee</sound> and squeaks, '<sound>Gee</sound>!'

拉.meaning: Divers haul an ancient <part>anchor</part> from the harbour and <part>stand</part> it upright on the dock. Carved down its shaft is an old motto that nobody can read, except the harbour's oldest parrot, who recites it every morning in perfect <kanji>Latin</kanji>.
拉.on: The dockers cheer the parrot with a '<sound>Rah</sound>-rah!' and it takes a bow.
拉.kun: '<sound>Rah</sound>-' it begins next morning, but a pirate scoops it up mid-word, perch and all, and rows away with it.

柵.meaning: A librarian runs out of shelves, so she plants each old <part>scroll</part> upright in the garden, lashing it to the next <part>tree</part> along. Soon a ring of rolled-up paper posts circles the library and keeps the goats out: a <kanji>stockade</kanji>.
柵.on: Inside it she grows one fat <sound>suc</sound>culent, the goats' favourite snack.
柵.kun: Vines entwine the posts: <sound>shee</sound>ts of ivy, then <sound>ga</sound>rlands of roses, and the librarian cheers, 'Hu<sound>rrah</sound>!'

慨.meaning: An old rock star's smartwatch shows his <part>heartbeat</part> slowing as he flips through photos of life <part>previously</part>: the crowds, the confetti, the shiny tour bus. He lets out a long, heavy sigh. All he can do now is <kanji>rue</kanji> it.
慨.on: His <sound>gui</sound>de dog rests its chin on his knee and sighs too.
慨.kun: '<sound>Nah</sound>,' he mutters, when a fan asks for a song, and <sound>ge</sound>ts back to his photo album.

憤.meaning: A grumpy park ranger's <part>heartbeat</part> pounds as tourists toss coins into the <part>geyser</part>. With every clink his temper rises like the steam, until both blow at once with a roar. His anger is well and truly <kanji>aroused</kanji>.
憤.on: His roar whips the coins up into the air like a little ty<sound>phoon</sound>.
憤.kun: Back home he slaps an <sound>ee</sound>l, a <sound>ki</sound>wi and a great lump of <sound>dough</sound> on the counter and kneads them all, still fuming.

旺.meaning: A <part>king</part> who hates paperwork moves his throne into a greenhouse under the <part>sun</part>. Moss grows on his crown, vines climb his robe, tomatoes ripen on his sceptre. The laws go unread, but his garden is <kanji>flourishing</kanji>.
旺.on: An acorn drops on his crown, and an <sound>oa</sound>k shoots up beside the throne.
旺.kun: A visiting queen in a <sound>sa</sound>ri parks her <sound>car</sound> among the tomatoes, and the king just hums, '<sound>Nn</sound>.'

硝.meaning: A sculptor carves a cave <part>stone</part> into the <part>resemblance</part> of her cat. In the damp, a white frost of tiny crystals creeps over its stone fur. She scrapes the crust into a jar and labels it saltpeter: <kanji>nitrate</kanji>.
硝.on: She takes the jar to a fireworks <sound>show</sound>, where it goes up with a bang.

淑.meaning: Your <part>uncle</part> takes up ballet at sixty. At the recital he leaps through a mist of <part>water drops</part> from the fog machine, lands without a sound on the tip of one toe, and bows. The whole hall gasps: he's <kanji>graceful</kanji>.
淑.on: Afterwards he sips his tea, little finger raised, and drops in one <sound>su</sound>gar <sound>cu</sound>be.
淑.kun: His dance partner joins him for the encore: <sound>she</sound> spins him round like a <sound>to</sound>p, and neither of them wobbles.

篤.meaning: A <part>horse</part> learns that the panda next door eats only <part>bamboo</part>. Every dawn, through storms and snow, she gallops to the far grove and back with one fresh shoot in her teeth. She never misses a day: her devotion is <kanji>fervent</kanji>.
篤.on: The panda sets its clock by her hooves: tick-<sound>tock</sound>, clip-clop.
篤.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>... <sound>tsu</sound>!' sneezes the panda, as the snowy horse shakes herself off at the door.

堪.meaning: A tiny seed under the <part>soil</part> gets <part>tremendously</part> squashed: a cow lies on it, a tractor parks on it, a circus elephant naps on it. Every spring it still pokes up one green leaf. That seed can <kanji>withstand</kanji> anything.
堪.on: Its roots dig a long <sound>tun</sound>nel under the whole farm.
堪.kun: A mole pops out of the tunnel and leaves the brave leaf a <sound>ta</sound>co as a prize.

熊.meaning: At a talent show, a huge furry contestant shows off every <part>ability</part>: juggling, tap dancing, then strolling barefoot across <part>hot coals</part> without a flinch. The judges wonder who's inside the costume, until he roars. It's a real <kanji>bear</kanji>.
熊.on: He wins first prize: a ride round the stage on a <sound>u</sound>nicorn.
熊.kun: He shares his prize <sound>coo</sound>kie with his <sound>ma</sound>ma in the front row.

該.meaning: In court, the judge gives a long <part>speech</part>: 'the said hoop', 'the said ladder', 'the said acrobat'. Each time, the <part>acrobat</part> in the dock flips and points at the very thing he means, so nobody forgets which one: the <kanji>above-stated</kanji> one.
該.on: A <sound>gui</sound>de dog in the public gallery nods along every time.

峠.meaning: A snail sets off over a <part>mountain</part>. For a week the path points <part>above</part>, inch after inch, then at the very top it tips <part>below</part>, and he slides the rest of the way on his shell, cheering. Where up turns into down is the <kanji>mountain pass</kanji>.
峠.kun: At the top, a hiker resting there stubs her <sound>toe</sound> on a sleeping <sound>ge</sound>cko.

娯.meaning: Every Friday the <part>woman</part> who runs the post office decides to <part>give</part> herself the afternoon off: kites, a jigsaw, a nap in a hammock. The sign on her door just says 'Gone for <kanji>recreation</kanji>'.
娯.on: This Friday it's snorkelling, so she packs her <sound>go</sound>ggles.

鍋.meaning: Every hour, the <part>cuckoo clock</part> in the kitchen pops open, but instead of a bird, a little <part>gold</part> spoon swings out and stirs the stew bubbling below. The stew has never once burned in that old <kanji>pot</kanji>.
鍋.on: Tonight's stew is a whole <sound>ca</sound>rp, its tail sticking out the top.
鍋.kun: <sound>Na</sound>na carries a steaming bowl of it up to <sound>be</sound>d.

暁.meaning: One morning the sleepy <part>sun</part> gets stuck in a factory <part>chimney</part> on its way up. The stokers push it from below with long brooms until it pops out like a cork, and the whole town glows pink: <kanji>daybreak</kanji>.
暁.on: The stokers celebrate with a plate of <sound>gyo</sound>za, warmed on the sun.
暁.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>,' sighs the sweep, shaking soot from his <sound>ca</sound>rdigan, sneezes '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' and peels a <sound>ki</sound>wi for breakfast.

釜.meaning: A <part>father</part> digs up a <part>gold</part> nugget in the garden. Instead of a new car, he has it beaten into a big round-bellied cooking pot for camping trips. It hangs over every campfire, and the family gathers round the shining <kanji>kettle</kanji>.
釜.on: At night he sleeps beside it on a rolled-out <sound>fu</sound>ton, guarding it.
釜.kun: 'Good <sound>karma</sound>,' he says, every time it boils.
